npcs.name: Nell Riverwick
npcs.description: A street sweep rooted at dawn streets with a rush broom, known for how she listens more than she sweeps.
npcs.biography: Nell did not plan to become the town's go-to street sweep, yet dawn streets with a rush broom made the choice sticky. Now 24, the Human measures success in quiet evenings and unpaid favors returned. She listens more than she sweeps, and keeps the pocket full of lost buttons she means to return like a confessor keeps secrets. Friend to Finn; informant to Merrick. Hope pulls one way—save for a room that doesn't leak—while caution pulls the other because of being noticed by the wrong people for noticing too much. Mapped which cellar grates glow after midnight for Merrick.
npcs.personality: Steady and sharp-eyed; listens more than she sweeps.
npcs.motivation: To save for a room that doesn't leak without feeding being noticed by the wrong people for noticing too much.
npcs.secret: Knows more about this than she admits: Mapped which cellar grates glow after midnight for Merrick.
npcs.rumor: A smugglers' mark was seen near dawn streets with a rush broom on a night Nell worked late.
npcs.voice: Low and practical, with a habit of repeating the important clause once.
npcs.appearance: A human silhouette framed by dawn streets with a rush broom, hands seldom empty of the pocket full of lost buttons she means to return.

relationships.note: Passes street details for tea money.

npcs.name: Jab Millroad
npcs.description: Jab holds down the mill road with his two-mule cart with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Walk into the mill road with his two-mule cart and you will find Jab Millroad before you find a free chair. A 38-year-old Human carter, Jab greets trouble the way other folk greet weather: with a coat and a plan. He names his mules after bad decisions. The waybill clipboard chewed at the corners travels with him almost everywhere. Hauls for Garr; drinks with Old Tallow. His ambition is to buy a covered wagon before winter rain. His nightmare is highway 'tolls' that aren't official. Right now, Was paid double to deliver an unmarked crate to the old mill and ask nothing.
npcs.personality: Warm with regulars, curt with wasters; names his mules after bad decisions.
npcs.motivation: Secure enough ground to buy a covered wagon before winter rain.
npcs.secret: Quietly arranging matters around: Was paid double to deliver an unmarked crate to the old mill and ask nothing.
npcs.rumor: Jab is writing a private list of debts the council will not touch.
npcs.voice: Polite public voice; sharper private asides when trust appears.
npcs.appearance: Looks like someone who sleeps lightly; distinctive detail is the waybill clipboard chewed at the corners.

npcs.name: Oma Kettle
npcs.description: A laundry worker rooted at the washhouse steam, known for how she hums lullabies to stained sheets.
npcs.biography: Oma learned the hard corners of town by working them as a laundry worker based out of the washhouse steam. At 70, the Halfling has a map of loyalties written in calluses rather than ink. Day after day she hums lullabies to stained sheets, and the cake of soap scented with river mint marks her place in the room. Washes for manor staff; knows Ora. Her north star is to see her grandson apprenticed cleanly. The shadow at her heels is illness spreading through shared basins. Found a blood-stiffened shirt with a Vale-colored thread in the cuff.

npcs.motivation: To see her grandson apprenticed cleanly without feeding illness spreading through shared basins.

npcs.name: Finn Cobble
npcs.description: Familiar face at shortcuts between market and manor; useful, stubborn, and hard to surprise.
npcs.biography: Finn learned the hard corners of town by working them as a messenger boy based out of shortcuts between market and manor. At 16, the Human has a map of loyalties written in calluses rather than ink. Day after day he runs messages before he reads them—usually, and the scuffed satchel with a false seam marks his place in the room. Idolizes Blink; friends with Nell. His north star is to become a long-road courier like Blink. The shadow at his heels is delivering something that gets a friend hanged. Peeked at a letter from Brother Caldus naming Magister Quen.
npcs.personality: Proud of competence more than praise; runs messages before he reads them—usually.
npcs.motivation: Protect his place at shortcuts between market and manor long enough to become a long-road courier like Blink.
npcs.secret: Has not told allies that peeked at a letter from Brother Caldus naming Magister Quen.
npcs.rumor: Finn is writing a private list of debts the council will not touch.
npcs.voice: Measured human cadence; concrete nouns before adjectives.
npcs.appearance: Work-worn human garb; scuffed satchel with a false seam always nearby.

relationships.note: Wants to become a real long-road courier.

npcs.name: Bera Wells
npcs.description: The well keeper people recommend when they actually want the job finished.
npcs.biography: Some townsfolk swear Bera was born mid-shift at the town well square; the truth is only slightly less devoted. This Human well keeper, now 52, treats competence like courtesy. She rations buckets fairly when drought talk starts, never far from the iron well key on a red cord. Community voice; speaks to Mayor Haldrin. Ask what she wants and she names it plainly: fund a second well before the next dry summer. Ask what she dreads and the answer is poison or panic at the water. Then comes the fresh problem—Noticed a bitter taste the morning after smugglers used the mill race.
npcs.personality: Soft-spoken until principles are poked; rations buckets fairly when drought talk starts.
npcs.motivation: Turn today's scrapes into tomorrow's chance to fund a second well before the next dry summer.
npcs.secret: Night thoughts keep returning to poison or panic at the water, especially since: Noticed a bitter taste the morning after smugglers used the mill race.
npcs.rumor: Someone paid Bera to forget a name connected to the town well square.
npcs.voice: Quick river-town diction, then sudden silences that mean more than words.
npcs.appearance: Easy to spot near the town well square: human, practical layers, and that iron well key on a red cord.

npcs.name: Skog Rake
npcs.description: Familiar face at the public stables; useful, stubborn, and hard to surprise.
npcs.biography: Skog did not plan to become the town's go-to stable hand, yet the public stables made the choice sticky. Now 33, the Half-Orc measures success in quiet evenings and unpaid favors returned. He speaks to horses before people, and keeps the curry comb worn to a crescent like a confessor keeps secrets. Stables Jor's caravan beasts; quiet friend to Vessa. Hope pulls one way—breed a courier line that outruns bandits—while caution pulls the other because of fire in the hayloft. Found a branded Vale mare stabled under a false name overnight.
npcs.personality: Proud of competence more than praise; speaks to horses before people.
npcs.motivation: Protect his place at the public stables long enough to breed a courier line that outruns bandits.
npcs.secret: Has not told allies that found a branded Vale mare stabled under a false name overnight.
npcs.rumor: Skog can open doors at the public stables after hours—if asked the right way.

npcs.description: Tilda holds down rooftops and chimneys with callused competence and open ears.
npcs.biography: Tilda learned the hard corners of town by working them as a chimney sweep based out of rooftops and chimneys. At 61, the Human has a map of loyalties written in calluses rather than ink. Day after day she spits soot and blessings in the same breath, and the rope harness inked with chimney marks marks her place in the room. Confirms Old Tallow's lantern story. Her north star is to train one apprentice who isn't afraid of heights. The shadow at her heels is falling through a rotten stack. Saw signal lanterns answering each other from mill to river from a roof ridge.

npcs.name: Wren Pocket
npcs.description: Familiar face at fountain steps with a peddler cloth; useful, stubborn, and hard to surprise.
npcs.biography: Wren Pocket's reputation as a street peddler was built one careful errand at a time around fountain steps with a peddler cloth. Age 40 sits lightly on this Gnome, except when old debts creak. Watch long enough and you will see that they turns jokes into discounts. The box of 'lucky' nails that are just nails is part tool, part talisman. Competes lightly with Quinn; knows Mouse. They would trade sleep to rent a real stall by spring, yet stays wary of Quinn undercutting their street trade. Current spark: Sold a 'treasure map' that Mouse Pip later swore matched real tunnels.
npcs.personality: Proud of competence more than praise; turns jokes into discounts.
npcs.motivation: Protect their place at fountain steps with a peddler cloth long enough to rent a real stall by spring.

npcs.name: Mael Ferry
npcs.description: Local dock hauler whose days orbit the cargo docks and small lasting loyalties.
npcs.biography: Before dawn touches the roofs, Mael is already at the cargo docks, working as a dock hauler with flour, ink, sweat, or steel still on his fingers from yesterday. The habit everyone notices is simple: he rolls shoulders before lifting anything proud. Close by sits his prized hooks and gloves stiff with river salt, a small anchor in a loud town. Works near Tem Brine; wary of Nedda. He wants to join a river crew with proper shares. He fears cranes failing on a crowded quay more than open confrontation. A usable adventure hook trails him: Helped Nedda unload 'grain' that smelled of lamp oil.
npcs.personality: Dry humor over a careful heart; rolls shoulders before lifting anything proud.
npcs.motivation: Finish one honest plan: join a river crew with proper shares.
npcs.secret: Keeps proof related to a problem—Helped Nedda unload 'grain' that smelled of lamp oil.
npcs.rumor: The hooks and gloves stiff with river salt once belonged to a person who vanished upriver.
npcs.voice: Storyteller rhythm even when discussing ledgers or latches.
npcs.appearance: Human features shaped by work at the cargo docks; watch for the hooks and gloves stiff with river salt.

npcs.name: Sera Patch
npcs.description: The seamstress people recommend when they actually want the job finished.
npcs.biography: Before dawn touches the roofs, Sera is already at a tiny mending shop by the lane, working as a seamstress with flour, ink, sweat, or steel still on her fingers from yesterday. The habit everyone notices is simple: she bites thread instead of using scissors when nervous. Close by sits her prized basket of orphaned buttons from Oma, a small anchor in a loud town. Friend to Pippa; customer of Issy. She wants to sew Pippa's first proper dress for a dance. She fears rent rising after Midsummer more than open confrontation. A usable adventure hook trails her: Mended a tear pattern that matched a climb over a spiked wall.

npcs.name: Yara Moss
npcs.description: Local herb gatherer whose days orbit the tree line beyond the north gate and small lasting loyalties.
npcs.biography: Yara Moss keeps the tree line beyond the north gate running with the stubborn patience of a 26-year-old Half-Elf who has already survived worse seasons than this one. She thanks plants before she cuts them, and the drying racks of labeled leaves is usually within reach when tempers rise. Supplies Petra; walks trails with Kavi. Her private aim is plain enough: publish a simple herbal for midwives. Still, she flinches at the thought of overharvesting a rare feverwort patch. Lately the trouble under her nose is this: Found bootprints and chalk arrows near her feverwort—heading toward the mill.
